The Honorable Rogers C. B. Morton Secretary of the Interior Washington, D. C.
The Honorable Earl L. Butz Secretary of Agriculture Washington, D. C.
Dear Secretary Morton and Secretary Butz:
The American Mining Congress, a national trade association whose membership is composed of U.S. companies that produce most of the nation's metals, coal, and industrial and agricultural minerals, wishes to bring to your attention its views regarding the proposed regulation of off-road vehicles.
As chairman of the Public Lands Committee of the American Mining Congress, I have reviewed the proposed implementation of Executive Order 11644 pertaining to the use of off-road vehicles on the public lands.
While reasonable regulations which do not prevent mineral development operations are not objectionable to the mining industry, the American Mining Congress objects to the stringent regulations currently under consideration since they would have the effect of hindering prospecting and mining of minerals on public lands. Any permit system to regulate the use of off-road vehicles used in mining would delay miners and most certainly discourage mineral exploration and development on public lands.
Regulations restricting use of off-road vehicles should be limited to recreational vehicles; the language of Executive Order 11644 indicates
